title: Prerequisites and Programming Fundamentals
subtopics: Variables, Logic, and Data as Core Concepts
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of prerequisites and programming fundamentals using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates prerequisites and programming fundamentals.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Prerequisites and Programming Fundamentals** as part of **Introduction to Kotlin**. Apply prerequisites and programming fundamentals by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—Understanding Algorithms and Instructions, Source Code, Compilation, and Execution, Variables, Logic, and Data as Core Concepts—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Clear fundamentals help you reason about program behavior before adding abstraction. Small input/output checks make syntax and control flow easier to debug.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Prerequisites and Programming Fundamentals removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates prerequisites and programming fundamentals. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving understanding algorithms and instructions.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain prerequisites and programming fundamentals without copying the lesson wording.
Demonstrate the concept with a small code/configuration change and state the expected result.
Test one boundary case or explain a relevant platform/version limitation.
hints: Begin with the first syllabus subtopic: Understanding Algorithms and Instructions. What input or state does it act on?
Change only one value, branch, declaration, or dependency at a time. Predict what should happen before running the code.
Compare your observed result with the expected output and the official reference; verify that you are using the required project type and dependency set.
